outcome: maternal morbidity indicators (antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum hemorrhage, caesarean hysterectomy, maternal ICU admission)
fetal morbidity parameters (prematurity, low birth weight, need for ICU admission)
cohort: The study involved 130 patients diagnosed with placenta previa, categorized into those with a previously scarred uterus and those with an unscarred uterus.
finding: Patients with placenta previa and a scarred uterus had significantly higher rates of antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum hemorrhage, caesarean hysterectomy, and maternal ICU admission compared to those with an unscarred uterus.
mod_finding: Previous LSCS was a significant cause of scarred uterus and was statistically associated with higher rates of caesarean hysterectomy and maternal ICU admission.
